## About this fork
Upstream provides the original theme framework, styling system, loader, settings infrastructure and
testing scaffolding. This fork focuses on replacing the contour animation subsystem.
The contour background is now rendered from a precomputed, seamlessly tileable terrain: the pattern
is drawn to a texture once, and scrolling only translates that texture. The previous engine deformed
the field and re-extracted its contour lines every frame, so it is replaced (with its frame-rate se
tting) rather than adjusted, and the contour settings now describe scroll direction, speed and densi
ng) rather than adjusted, and the contour settings now describe scroll direction, speed and density.
Implementation details, the defects found while building it and their measurements are in docs/engin
eering-notes.md; the full change list is in CHANGELOG.md.

## Features
Everything lives in **Settings › Endfield Theme Settings**:

- master switch; palette (Valley Yellow / Wuling Cyan); radius (square / round);
- contour backgroun
d, contour scroll switch, scroll direction (8 directions), scroll speed (`12 / 24 / 48 / 96 / 192` p
x/s), contour density (sparse / medium / dense / very dense), terrain roughness (**a 12-stop slider:
plains → hills → high mountains, stacking plateaus / cliffs / ridge lines / deep valleys / water an

nimation;
- thunder title, and its entrance animation.
Behaviour worth knowing:
- scroll speed is in **pixels per second** and advances with the real frame interval, so it looks th

e same at 60 / 120 / 144 / 240 Hz;
- changing direction or speed only updates two cached numbers; ch
anging density re-extracts contours from the **same** terrain; changing terrain roughness regenerate
s the terrain from the **same seed** (low stops are flat plains, high stops are rugged high mountain
s; plateaus appear at stop 6 and shrink to none by stop 10, cliffs start at stop 8 and are heaviest
at stop 12; landform strengths grow along a convex curve so the steps near the top buy the most, and

stop 12 covers about 61% of the sheet while no landform layer ever passes the 75% ceiling);
- a new
random terrain is generated each time the contour background is switched on, and the same seed and

size always reproduce the same terrain within a session;
- `prefers-reduced-motion` is read live: wi
th it on, the pattern renders statically.
Settings are persisted through DSH's settings namespace (host `index.js` registers it, the browser h
alf reads/writes it through `ctx.settingsScope`), so they survive restarts and port changes and work
in DSH Desktop. UI text follows the DSH language setting (Chinese / English).
## Compatibility
Tested environment:

- DSH: **0.1.1-rc.2**
- Profile: `web`
- Platform: Windows
Other DSH versions have not been tested and may not work correctly; future DSH releases may require
migration, especially if the settings API, bundle-row format or client bundle loader changes.
This fork is a **separate package** (`dsh-theme-endfield-contour-rework`) with its own settings name
space, so it can be installed next to upstream without clobbering it. Because the namespace differs,
**upstream settings do not carry over** — the fork starts from its own defaults. Both plugins also
drive the same `<body>` classes, so enabling both at once is not recommended; disable upstream if yo
u install this fork.
Two bounds on the pattern itself: the texture is capped at 4096 device pixels per side and 8.3e6 CSS
px² (on very large canvases the pattern repeats more often), and the OS "reduce motion" setting ren
canvases the pattern repeats more often), and the OS "reduce motion" setting renders it statically.
